newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Labour Party embraces privatisation - papers.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Labour Party embraces privatisation - papers.

text.p: Britain's main opposition Labour Party is set to embrace a policy of privatising remaining state assets in a break from its traditional stance, Sunday newspapers reported.

The Sunday Telegraph said Labour leader Tony Blair would use a speech to businessmen on Monday to stress that if his party won the May 1 general election, its "presumption" would be "that economic activity is best left to the private sector".
The paper said Blair would endorse the privatisation strategy pursued successfully by the ruling Conservatives over the past 18 years.
Labour officials were quoted as confirming the party was now prepared to match Conservative promises and sell off Royal Mail agencies such as Parcelforce, the Post Office's parcel distribution arm.

Blair would say in his speech: "Where there is no over-riding reason for preferring public provision of goods and services -- particularly where those services operate in a competitive market -- then the presumption should be that economic activity is best left to the private sector, with market forces being encoraged to operate."
The Sunday Times said if Labour won the election, it would conduct an urgent review of all government services, land and buildings with a view to selling assets worth billions of pounds (dollars).
The paper said Labour also planned to go back on concessions to trade unions in order to head off further damaging Conservative attacks in the election campaign.
The Conservatives said the reports showed Labour was now "in full retreat".
Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine said: "The Labour Party have opposed each and every one of the privatisations which this government has brought forward over the past 18 years.
"Now Mr Blair, the man who has put trust at the heart of this election, is casting aside his principles like ballast from his sinking balloon."
